newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran holds nationwide anti-Israel rallies.
newsitem.headline: Iran holds nationwide anti-Israel rallies.

text.p: Large crowds chanting "Death to Israel" and "Death to America" marched in Tehran on Friday and heard President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani denounce Israel as a "dragon" created by the West.

Men and black-clad women marched to Tehran University for mass prayers carrying placards reading "Israel is a cancerous tumour" and pictures of Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini and his successor Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The march was part of rallies held across Iran to mark "World Qods (Jerusalem) Day", the last Friday of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan dedicated to protests against the Jewish state by Khomeini in 1979.
Demonstrators, marching from six separate assembly points in Tehran, stepped on Israeli flags laid on street pavements and burned a large map of the Jewish state.

In an emotional sermon during which he appeared to be near tears at times, Rafsanjani condemned Israel for "atrocities" against Palestinian civilians and blasted the United States for supporting the Jewish state.

"Westerners created this dragon (Israel) with the main aim of cutting up the Islamic world, pressuring Moslems and protecting Western interests," Rafsanjani said in the sermon broadcast on state-run Tehran radio.

"Jerusalem is the main issue in the Islamic world today. I hope the holiness of Jerusalem and the Moslem nations' love for this holy place will arouse the wrath of the peoples of the Islamic countries and create new conditions," he said.
A resolution read at the rally said: "The liberation of Jerusalem and its return into Islam's bosom is only possible through armed struggle and a united anti-Zionist front", the radio reported.
Speaking before Rafsanjani, parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri blasted Israel as a "bastard" state.

"The only path to salvation is to struggle, resist and wage war. May God give you (Palestinians) victory. I hope one day we will celebrate your victory and the destruction of Israel," Nateq-Nouri said.
The Iranian news agency IRNA said rallies were also held in areas in northeastern Iran hit by two strong quakes on Tuesday which killed at least 79 people.
Iran says Israel has no right to exist. Tehran has strongly condemned the Middle East peace process as a sellout of Palestinian amd Islamic rights.
